cards.front: Recall a key point about Erosion, Transport & Deposition
cards.back: Erosion is the removal and transport of weathered material by rivers, wind, ice and gravity

cards.front: Recall a key point about Erosion, Transport & Deposition
cards.back: River erosion processes: hydraulic action (force of water), abrasion (sediment scraping bedrock), attrition (particles rounding), solution (dissolving)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Erosion, Transport & Deposition
cards.back: Transport methods: traction (rolling large particles), saltation (bouncing), suspension (fine particles carried in water), solution (dissolved load)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Erosion, Transport & Deposition
cards.back: Deposition occurs when the transporting agent loses energy: river slows (inside of meander, floodplain), glacier melts, wind drops

cards.front: Recall a key point about Erosion, Transport & Deposition
cards.back: Glacial erosion: plucking (freezing onto rock and pulling fragments), abrasion (rock-laden ice scouring bedrock, producing striations)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Erosion, Transport & Deposition
cards.back: Wind erosion and deposition: deflation (removing fine material), abrasion (sand-blasting), loess (wind-blown silt deposits)

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — erosion, transport & deposition?
cards.back: 1. For Erosion, Transport & Deposition questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3. For evaluation, weigh competing geological theories with evidence
